chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, who said: Mufazzal ibn Salih narrated to me from Maysar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

He said: His visit to this House (of God) shall not be accepted if he does not possess three characteristics: piety that restrains him from the sins of Allah the Exalted, forbearance by which he controls his anger, and good companionship with those he accompanies.

key_terms.حُسْنُ الصَّحَابَةِ: Good companionship or pleasant company with others
key_terms.حِلْمٌ: Forbearance or patience that controls anger
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: Piety or God-consciousness that restrains one from sin
key_terms.يَعْبَأُ: To care for or accept (in the negative context: to not accept)

ai.seo_question: What three characteristics must a pilgrim possess for their visit to the Kaaba to be accepted?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) emphasizes that the spiritual validity of Hajj hinges not merely on ritual performance but on the pilgrim's internal character, specifically piety (*war'*), forbearance (*hilm*), and virtuous companionship (*husn al-sahabah*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* and moral refinement as prerequisites for the acceptance of acts of worship, linking the physical act of visiting the Kaaba with the purification of the soul and social conduct.
